c.tagline: Fog-wrapped hills, tech dreams, Golden Gate.

taxi.color: White with company markings (no single color); rideshare-dominant

emergency.note: Dial 311 for non-emergency city services; English-speaking operators are standard.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Mission District: Mission Dolores, the city's oldest building, plus Balmy Alley murals
hood_landmark.Haight-Ashbury: the iconic Haight and Ashbury intersection of 1960s counterculture fame
hood_landmark.Chinatown: the Dragon Gate at Grant Avenue and Bush Street
hood_landmark.The Castro: the Castro Theatre's landmark neon marquee

avoid.reason: The Tenderloin and parts of SoMa/Mid-Market have open drug use and aggressive panhandling day and night.

hood_desc: The Mission is a lively, sunny, historically Latino neighborhood packed with taquerias, murals, dive bars and trendy restaurants, great for foodies, young creatives and nightlife seekers.

Haight-Ashbury is the storied birthplace of 1960s hippie counterculture, now a bohemian strip of vintage clothing shops, record stores and Victorians beside Golden Gate Park, appealing to music lovers and free spirits.
Nob Hill is an elegant, hilly enclave of grand historic hotels, cathedrals and cable cars with sweeping views, suiting upscale travelers who want refined, quiet surroundings near downtown.
Chinatown is one of the oldest and busiest Chinatowns in North America, a dense warren of dim sum halls, herb shops and temples that draws visitors wanting authentic food and cultural immersion.

The Castro is the world-famous heart of LGBTQ life in San Francisco, a vibrant, welcoming district of rainbow flags, bars, cafes and the historic Castro Theatre, ideal for the queer community and open-minded visitors.

water.note: Tap water is safe and known for its high quality Hetch Hetchy source.

transit.pay: The Clipper card works on BART, Muni, ferries and more - get it free in Apple/Google Wallet or as a plastic card ($3) from station machines and Walgreens. Contactless tap-to-pay with your own bank card is also rolling out across Muni and BART. Cable cars cost $8 a ride (Clipper, app, or cash to the conductor).
transit.hours: BART runs about 5am-midnight (from 6am Sat, 8am Sun); Muni runs roughly 5am-midnight with 24-hour Owl bus routes; cable cars about 7am-10:30pm.

transit.m: BART train direct to downtown (~30 min)
